lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. The researcher found nothing because the WebSearch budget was exhausted, and my own WebSearch was refused for the same reason. A guessed Invaluable artist URL returned an empty 'undefined' page, and two Bing fetches gave no relevant results. No currency used.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so no maximum bid. Dickerson is a well-known Australian artist, but this is a late impression (59/60) from an edition of 60, and his prints are far more common than his paintings. I have not verified any market level for this print, so it stays a near miss until comps can be searched.
lots.confidence_reason: The signature and edition number are read in the photos, but there is no price evidence at all. The title is only partly legible.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 4 enlarged: pencil 'R. Dickerson' lower right, a fluent hand consistent with his print signature. Photo 3: '59/60' lower left. Two figures (nude from behind, figure in a bodysuit) in blue aquatint with an etched line. Plate margin visible inside a cream mat. Pale grey frame.
lots.condition: The visible image and margin look clean, with no foxing, tears or stains seen. There is slight light speckling in the aquatint ground (normal). The mat hides the sheet edges. Back, glazing and any mat burn or fading were not seen.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you show the back of the frame (any gallery or publisher label), and confirm there is no fading, foxing or mat burn to the sheet under the mat? Is the glass intact?

lots.working: Only SOLD entries within 24 months that are close (same artist, same medium, similar size) count. The one that qualifies is In the Looking Glass, AUD 4,400 (June 2025). keep_max_hammer = 4,400 / 1.198 = 3,672.8, rounded down to 3,670. Flip: likely resale about AUD 4,400 through Colville or Gibson's, less a vendor commission of about 20% (plus photography and insurance fees) = 3,520, less about $30 local delivery = 3,490. 3,490 / 2.396 = 1,456.6, rounded down to 1,455. The current Gowans bid is already $1,525 (2 bids, seen 30/09/2026), which is above the flip maximum, so treat this as a keep only. Caution: this rests on a single close comp. Its soldAmount may or may not include premium. The artist's own verso label gives a retail price well below recent auction results, and older small panels sold for $1,400 to $2,300 (2024), so a bid near the keep maximum is at the top of the evidence.

lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2: painted signature 'M-McWILLIAMS.' in his usual capital style. Photos 5 and 6: an 'Artist and Art Work Details' form taped verso, reading Michael McWilliams, 21 Norfolk St Perth, phone number, title The Heavenly Grass Hotel, acrylic on Australian cedar, 27 March 12, retail price $1,000, circled 96. lots.condition: Good overall. Small paint chips and wear along the top edge of the painted border (photo 3), plus minor edge rubbing. Image surface looks clean.
